title.zh: 卷328 列傳一百十五 常青 蓝元枚 蔡攀龙 梁朝桂 普吉保 丁朝雄 鄂辉 舒亮
title.en: Volume 328 Biographies 115: Chang Qing, Lan Yuanmei, Cai Panlong, Liang Chaogui, Pu Ji Bao, Ding Chaoxiong, E Hui, Shu Liang
title.raw: 卷328 列傳一百十五 常青 蓝元枚 蔡攀龙 梁朝桂 普吉保 丁朝雄 鄂辉 舒亮

sentences.zh: 列傳一百十五

translations.literal: Biographies 115
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 115

sentences.zh: 常青，佟佳氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Chang Qing, of the Tongjia clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Qing, of the Tongjia clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 父安圖，官至江西巡撫。

translations.literal: His father Antu rose to the post of Jiangxi governor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Antu had served as governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 常青自寧郡王府長史累遷察哈爾都統，杭州、福州將軍。

translations.literal: Chang Qing rose in succession from chief steward of the Prince of Ning's establishment to Chahar commandant and to general at Hangzhou and Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Qing advanced from chief steward of the Prince of Ning's household through the Chahar commandancy to the generalships at Hangzhou and Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十一年，署閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of the Qianlong reign, he served as acting governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1786 he was appointed acting governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 諸羅縣民楊光勳與其弟爭家業，糾眾立會，縣吏捕治不服，常青令按察使李永祺往按。

translations.literal: A Zhuluo county commoner named Yang Guangxun quarreled with his younger brother over the family estate, gathered a crowd to form a society, and when county officials arrested and punished them they would not submit; Chang Qing ordered the provincial surveillance commissioner Li Yongqi to go and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When a Zhuluo county man named Yang Guangxun feuded with his brother over their inheritance, rallied a crowd into a secret society, and resisted arrest, Chang Qing dispatched the surveillance commissioner Li Yongqi to investigate.

sentences.zh: 上以台灣在海外，不可輕縱，諭勿使蔓延疏脫。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering that Taiwan lay beyond the sea and must not be treated lightly, instructed that the affair must not be allowed to spread or slip through lax handling.
translations.idiomatic: Because Taiwan lay overseas and could not be handled lightly, the emperor ordered that the trouble must neither spread nor be allowed to slip away through negligence.

sentences.zh: 尋實授閩浙總督。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he received the substantive appointment as governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon confirmed in the governorship of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，林爽文亂起，陷彰化，知縣俞峻死之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the rebellion of Lin Shuangwen broke out; Zhanghua fell, and the magistrate Yu Jun died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Lin Shuangwen's rebellion erupted; the rebels took Zhanghua, and Magistrate Yu Jun was killed.

sentences.zh: 常青檄水師提督黃仕簡自鹿耳門進，副將丁朝雄從海壇鎮總兵郝壯猷自淡水進，都司馬元勳屯鹿仔港，分道部署；

translations.literal: Chang Qing issued orders for the naval commander Huang Shijian to advance from Lukang, for the brigade commander Ding Chaoxiong to advance with Haitan garrison commander Hao Zhuangyou from Tamsui, and for the company commander Ma Yuanxun to hold Lukang Harbor, deploying forces along separate routes;
translations.idiomatic: Chang Qing directed Naval Commander Huang Shijian to advance through Lukang, Brigadier Ding Chaoxiong and Haitan Garrison Commander Hao Zhuangyou to move inland from Tamsui, and Company Commander Ma Yuanxun to hold Lukang Harbor, dividing his forces accordingly;

sentences.zh: 復如泉州會陸路提督任承恩調度，令金門鎮總兵羅英笈詣廈門彈壓。

translations.literal: He then went to Quanzhou to confer with the land-force commander Ren Chengen on overall disposition, and ordered Kinmen garrison commander Luo Yingji to proceed to Xiamen to suppress unrest.
translations.idiomatic: He then met Land Commander Ren Chengen at Quanzhou to coordinate operations and sent Kinmen Garrison Commander Luo Yingji to Xiamen to keep order.

sentences.zh: 尋復令承恩自鹿耳門繼進。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again ordered Chengen to continue the advance from Lukang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon ordered Chengen to press forward again through Lukang.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，奏賊陷諸羅。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he memorialized that the rebels had taken Zhuluo.
translations.idiomatic: In 1787 he reported that the rebels had captured Zhuluo.

sentences.zh: 台灣鎮總兵柴大紀堵剿，賊勢稍沮。

translations.literal: Taiwan garrison commander Chai Daji blocked and pursued them in suppression, and the rebel strength was somewhat checked.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan Garrison Commander Chai Daji held the line and harried the rebels, and their momentum slackened somewhat.

sentences.zh: 爽文漳州人，其徒率漳籍。

translations.literal: Shuangwen was a native of Zhangzhou, and his followers were for the most part men of Zhangzhou registration.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen came from Zhangzhou, and most of his followers were Zhangzhou men.

sentences.zh: 移會兩廣督臣防範，上責其張皇。

translations.literal: He sent a circular to the governor of Guangdong and Guangxi to take precautions, and the emperor rebuked him for alarmism.
translations.idiomatic: He notified the governor-general of the Two Guangs to guard against spillover, but the emperor criticized him for overstating the danger.

sentences.zh: 授李侍堯閩浙總督，而移常青湖廣。

translations.literal: Li Shiyao was appointed governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang, while Chang Qing was transferred to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiyao was made governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang, and Chang Qing was transferred to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 既又命常青渡台視師，四月，至台灣。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was again ordered to cross to Taiwan to take command in person, and in the fourth month he arrived in Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered back to Taiwan to take personal command, reaching the island in the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 劾仕簡、承恩遷延觀望，擁兵自衛；

translations.literal: He impeached Shijian and Chengen for delay and watchful hesitation, hoarding troops for their own protection;
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Shijian and Chengen for dithering on the sidelines while keeping their troops for self-protection;

sentences.zh: 壯猷守鳳山，賊至，棄城走。

translations.literal: Zhuangyou was defending Fengshan; when the rebels arrived he abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangyou was holding Fengshan, but when the rebels came he abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 諭逮承恩，罷仕簡候命，而誅壯猷，遂授常青為將軍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chengen arrested, Shijian dismissed pending further orders, and Zhuangyou executed; Chang Qing was then appointed general.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Chengen arrested, Shijian suspended pending further orders, and Zhuangyou executed; Chang Qing was then made commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 賊攻府城，常青督諸軍禦戰，有所俘馘；

translations.literal: When the rebels attacked the prefectural city, Chang Qing directed the armies in defense and took some captives and heads;
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels assaulted the prefectural seat, Chang Qing led the armies in defense and won some captives and heads;

sentences.zh: 賊攻桶盤棧，令游擊蔡攀龍等分駐力禦。

translations.literal: when the rebels attacked Tongpan Stockade he ordered the brigade commander Cai Panlong and others to take up separate posts and resist with full force.
translations.idiomatic: when they attacked Tongpan Stockade he stationed Brigade Commander Cai Panlong and others at separate points to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 奏入，上以常青年逾七十，能如此勇往督戰，手詔嘉獎，授其子刑部筆帖式喜明三等侍衛，馳驛往省，並賜御用搬指。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor, noting that Chang Qing was over seventy yet could press forward so boldly to direct battle, personally wrote an edict of praise, appointed his son Ximing, a clerical officer in the Ministry of Justice, as a third-rank imperial bodyguard, sent him by urgent relay to visit his father, and also bestowed an imperial thumb ring.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor praised Chang Qing—already past seventy—for leading the fight in person, wrote him a personal commendation, made his son Ximing, a Ministry of Justice clerk, a third-rank imperial guardsman, sent him posthaste to visit his father, and granted Chang Qing an imperial thumb ring.

sentences.zh: 旋奏爽文還大里杙舊巢，其徒莊大田等萬餘人分擾南路，擬先南剿大田，乃北取爽文。

translations.literal: He soon memorialized that Shuangwen had returned to his old lair at Dali, that his followers Zhuang Datian and others, more than ten thousand men, were harrying the southern route in separate bands, and that he planned first to suppress Datian in the south and then move north against Shuangwen.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported that Shuangwen had withdrawn to his old base at Dali, that Zhuang Datian and more than ten thousand rebels were raiding the south, and that he intended to crush Datian in the south before turning north on Shuangwen.

sentences.zh: 上韙之，下部優敘。

translations.literal: The emperor approved the plan and ordered preferential commendation entered in the records.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan and ordered that his merits be specially recorded.

sentences.zh: 旋奏勦賊南潭，殲賊六百餘；

translations.literal: He soon memorialized that in suppressing the rebels at Nantan more than six hundred had been destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported a campaign at Nantan in which more than six hundred rebels were killed;

sentences.zh: 爽文之徒莊錫舍出降，擒偽軍師番婦金孃，請檻車送京師，上命授錫舍守備。

translations.literal: Shuangwen's follower Zhuang Xishe came over in surrender; the false strategist, the aboriginal woman Jin Niang, was captured, and he requested that she be sent to the capital in a caged cart; the emperor ordered Xishe appointed garrison commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen's follower Zhuang Xishe defected, and the rebels' aboriginal woman strategist Jin Niang was taken; he asked to send her to the capital in a prison cart, and the emperor made Xishe a garrison commandant.

sentences.zh: 又奏進剿鳳山，出城未十里，賊三面並進，官兵奮勇擊退；

translations.literal: He again memorialized on the advance against Fengshan: before the army had gone ten li beyond the city the rebels pressed in from three sides, and the government troops fought them off with spirited effort;
translations.idiomatic: He also reported an advance on Fengshan: less than ten li outside the city the rebels attacked from three sides, and the troops drove them back;

sentences.zh: 賊勢蔓延，請厚集兵力，遣大臣督戰。

translations.literal: as the rebel strength spread he requested a heavy concentration of forces and the dispatch of a high minister to direct the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: as the rebellion spread he asked for heavier forces and a senior minister to take command.

sentences.zh: 上命陝甘總督福康安往視師。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general Fuk'anggan to go and take command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Fuk'anggan to take command.

sentences.zh: 旋奏：「賊犯府城，為丁朝雄擊退。

translations.literal: He soon memorialized: "The rebels attacked the prefectural city and were beaten back by Ding Chaoxiong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported: "The rebels assaulted the prefectural seat and were repulsed by Ding Chaoxiong.

sentences.zh: 官軍攻莊大田於南潭，殺賊二百餘。

translations.literal: The government army attacked Zhuang Datian at Nantan and killed more than two hundred rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces attacked Zhuang Datian at Nantan and killed more than two hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 大營距府城未遠，勢相犄角，無後顧之虞。

translations.literal: The main camp was not far from the prefectural city, the positions mutually supporting like horn and corner, with no worry for the rear.
translations.idiomatic: The main camp lay close enough to the prefectural seat to support it like pincers, with no danger to the rear.

sentences.zh: 」得旨嘉獎，賜雙眼孔雀翎。

translations.literal: " He received an edict of praise and was granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor commended him and granted him the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 旋迭奏鹽水港、笨港均為賊據，糧道既斷，諸羅勢甚危；

translations.literal: He soon sent repeated memorials that Yanshui Harbor and Bengang were both held by rebels, the grain route was cut, and the situation at Zhuluo was extremely perilous;
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported repeatedly that Yanshui Harbor and Bengang had fallen to the rebels, supplies were cut off, and Zhuluo was in grave danger;

sentences.zh: 令總兵魏大斌赴援，戰賊失利，又令游擊田藍玉援大斌。

translations.literal: he ordered the commander Wei Dabin to go to the relief, but in fighting the rebels Dabin was defeated, and he then ordered the brigade commander Tian Lanyu to reinforce Dabin.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Commander Wei Dabin to relieve the city, but Dabin was beaten in action, so he dispatched Brigade Commander Tian Lanyu to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 上以兵分力薄，飭常青調度失當。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering that the forces were divided and too thin, rebuked Chang Qing for faulty disposition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed Chang Qing for spreading his forces too thin and mishandling the campaign.

sentences.zh: 又諭：「常青駐軍桶盤棧，距南潭不過五里，不將賊目莊大田先行剿除，乃結營自守。

translations.literal: He further instructed: "Chang Qing is encamped at Tongpan Stockade, no more than five li from Nantan, yet instead of first destroying the rebel leader Zhuang Datian he has fortified a camp and merely holds his ground.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Chang Qing holds Tongpan Stockade only five li from Nantan, yet instead of destroying the rebel chief Zhuang Datian first he has dug in and merely defended himself.

sentences.zh: 肘腋之間，任其逼處。

translations.literal: At his very armpit he allows the enemy to press close.
translations.idiomatic: He has let the enemy press in under his very arm.

sentences.zh: 八月，命福康安為將軍，督諸將海蘭察、普爾普等大出師討爽文。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Fuk'anggan was appointed general and directed the commanders Hailancha, Pu'erpu, and others in a major expedition against Shuangwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Fuk'anggan was made commander-in-chief and led Hailancha, Pu'erpu, and other generals in a major campaign against Shuangwen.

sentences.zh: 諭常青，謂：「非責其師無功，特以年已七十，軍旅非所素習。

translations.literal: An edict was sent to Chang Qing, saying: "This is not to blame you for failure in command; it is only that you are already seventy, and military affairs are not what you have long practiced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Chang Qing: "This is not to blame you for failing in command; you are seventy, and warfare has never been your specialty.

sentences.zh: 福康安未至，仍當相機進​​剿。

translations.literal: Before Fuk'anggan arrives you should still advance and suppress as circumstances permit."
translations.idiomatic: Until Fuk'anggan arrives you should still press the attack as opportunity allows."

sentences.zh: 」旋奏：「賊自南潭來攻，侍衛烏什哈達等擊敗之。

translations.literal: " He soon memorialized: "The rebels attacked from Nantan and were defeated by the bodyguard Ushihada and others.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported: "Rebels advanced from Nantan and were beaten back by the guardsman Ushihada and others.

sentences.zh: 因雨後路滑，收兵；

translations.literal: Because the roads were slippery after rain, the troops were withdrawn;
translations.idiomatic: After rain made the roads treacherous, the troops were withdrawn;

sentences.zh: 又進攻南潭，焚草藔數百間，以天晚，山徑偪仄，不便深入。

translations.literal: they again attacked Nantan and burned several hundred grass huts; as night fell the mountain paths were narrow and cramped, making a deep advance inconvenient."
translations.idiomatic: they attacked Nantan again and burned several hundred rebel huts; night fell, the mountain paths were narrow, and a deep pursuit was impracticable."

sentences.zh: 」藔謂賊所居草屋也。

translations.literal: " Cao here means the grass huts in which the rebels dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: Cao here means the grass huts in which the rebels lived.

sentences.zh: 上以其屢稱遇雨路仄收兵，傳旨嚴飭。

translations.literal: Because he repeatedly cited rain and narrow roads as reasons for withdrawing troops, an edict was sent sternly rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Because he kept citing rain and bad roads as excuses for pulling back, the emperor sent a stern reprimand.

sentences.zh: 上又聞賊诇知軍中暑濕多病，常青機事不密，又不督兵深入，屢詰責。

translations.literal: The emperor also heard that the rebels had spied out how the army suffered from heat, damp, and widespread illness, that Chang Qing was not tight in keeping plans secret, and that he again failed to drive the troops deep; he was repeatedly called to account.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the rebels had discovered the army's heat-sickness and that Chang Qing was leaky in counsel and still would not drive a deep offensive, the emperor rebuked him again and again.

sentences.zh: 旋奏總兵梁朝桂勦賊多斬獲，提督柴大紀報諸羅圍急，令副將蔡攀龍赴援。

translations.literal: He soon memorialized that the commander Liang Chaogui had suppressed the rebels with many kills and captures; the commander-in-chief Chai Daji reported that the siege of Zhuluo was urgent, and he ordered the deputy commander Cai Panlong to go to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that Commander Liang Chaogui had killed many rebels, that Commander-in-Chief Chai Daji warned that Zhuluo's siege was critical, and that he had sent Deputy Commander Cai Panlong to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 上諭令親援大紀，待福康安至，合軍進攻。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him to go in person to relieve Daji and, when Fuk'anggan arrived, to join forces for a combined attack.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to relieve Daji in person and, once Fuk'anggan arrived, to combine forces for a general assault.

sentences.zh: 旋奏同江寧將軍永慶等在竹篙厝等處殲賊甚眾；

translations.literal: He soon memorialized that together with the Jiangning general Yongqing and others he had destroyed a great many rebels at Zhugecuo and other places;
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported that he and Jiangning General Yongqing had destroyed large numbers of rebels at Zhugecuo and elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 山豬毛社義民尤趫捷，獲砲一，生擒賊目張招。

translations.literal: the militia of the Shanzhumao community were especially swift, one cannon was captured, and the rebel leader Zhang Zhao was taken alive.
translations.idiomatic: the Shanzhumao militia proved especially agile, one cannon was taken, and rebel leader Zhang Zhao was captured alive.

sentences.zh: 又奏總兵普吉保克月眉莊，距諸羅五里，令與大紀並力固守；

translations.literal: he again memorialized that the commander Pu Jibao had taken Yuemeizhuang, five li from Zhuluo, and he ordered him to hold firm together with Daji;
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that Commander Pu Jibao had taken Yuemeizhuang, five li from Zhuluo, and ordered him to hold the line with Daji;

sentences.zh: 又令諸生劉宗榮等給番社土目札諭防賊竄匿。

translations.literal: he also ordered the licentiate Liu Zongrong and others to issue written notices to the aboriginal headmen of the fan communities to guard against rebels slipping into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: and he had licentiate Liu Zongrong and others issue notices to aboriginal village headmen to block rebel hideouts.

sentences.zh: 屢得旨嘉許。

translations.literal: He repeatedly received edicts of approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 福康安渡台灣。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan crossed to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan crossed to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 上授常青福州將軍，留辦善後，令從將軍職戴單眼孔雀翎。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Chang Qing general at Fuzhou, left him to handle postwar settlement, and allowed him to retain the general's rank while wearing the single-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Chang Qing Fuzhou general, left him to manage the aftermath, and let him keep his commander's rank with the single-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 福康安劾大紀貪劣狀，上責常青徇隱，奪職，交福康安嚴鞫。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan impeached Daji for corruption and misconduct; the emperor blamed Chang Qing for shielding him, stripped his office, and handed him over to Fuk'anggan for strict interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuk'anggan impeached Daji for corruption, the emperor blamed Chang Qing for covering for him, stripped his post, and handed him to Fuk'anggan for investigation.

sentences.zh: 福康安旋以常青自承徇隱，請交部治罪，上特宥之。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan soon reported that Chang Qing had himself confessed to shielding Daji and asked that he be handed to the ministry for punishment; the emperor specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan reported that Chang Qing had confessed to shielding Daji and asked the ministry to punish him, but the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 召詣京師，署鑲紅旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital and served as acting commander of the Mongol Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital and made acting commander of the Mongol Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，授禮部尚書、鑲藍旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he was appointed minister of rites and commander of the Han Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1789 he was appointed minister of rites and commander of the Han Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，卒，諡恭簡。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he died, and was given the posthumous title Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1793 and was posthumously titled Gongjian, "Respectful and Simple."

sentences.zh: 子喜明，官至徐州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: His son Ximing rose to garrison commander at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ximing rose to garrison commander at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 常青初視師，福州將軍恆瑞，水陸二提督任承恩、黃仕簡皆在行，戰無功。

translations.literal: When Chang Qing first took command, the Fuzhou general Heng Rui and the two commanders of land and naval forces, Ren Chengen and Huang Shijian, were all in the field, yet the fighting achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Qing first took command, Fuzhou General Heng Rui and the land and naval commanders Ren Chengen and Huang Shijian were all in the field, yet they won nothing.

sentences.zh: 承恩、仕簡以誤軍機坐斬，台灣平，赦出獄。

translations.literal: Chengen and Shijian were sentenced to death for military failure; when Taiwan was pacified they were pardoned and released from prison.
translations.idiomatic: Chengen and Shijian had been condemned to death for dereliction; after Taiwan was pacified they were pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 仕簡至狼山鎮總兵，承恩亦至副將，恆瑞自有傳。

translations.literal: Shijian rose again to garrison commander at Langshan, Chengen also to deputy commander; Heng Rui has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shijian eventually became Langshan garrison commander and Chengen a deputy commander; Heng Rui has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 藍元枚，字簡侯，福建漳浦人，提督廷珍孫。

translations.literal: Lan Yuanmei, style Jianhou, was a native of Zhangpu in Fujian and grandson of the commander Lan Tingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Yuanmei, styled Jianhou, came from Zhangpu in Fujian and was the grandson of Commander Lan Tingzhen.

sentences.zh: 父日寵，官福建銅山營水師參將。

translations.literal: His father Richong held the post of naval deputy commander of the Tongshan garrison in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Richong had been naval deputy commander of the Tongshan garrison in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 元枚襲三等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: Yuanmei inherited the hereditary rank of third-class commandant of light chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmei inherited the hereditary rank of third-class commandant of light chariots.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年，命發廣東，以外海水師參將用，補海門營參將。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of the Qianlong reign he was ordered to proceed to Guangdong and, employed as a coastal naval deputy commander, was appointed deputy commander of the Haimen garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1766 he was sent to Guangdong as a coastal naval deputy commander and appointed to the Haimen garrison.

sentences.zh: 累遷總兵，歷台灣、金門、蘇松三鎮。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to garrison commander, serving in the three garrisons of Taiwan, Kinmen, and Susong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the garrison commands at Taiwan, Kinmen, and Susong.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，授江南提督。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he was appointed commander of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1784 he was made commander of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 五十二年正月，台灣民林爽文為亂，命元枚馳驛往泉州，署福建陸路提督，駐蚶江策應。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifty-second year the Taiwan commoner Lin Shuangwen rose in rebellion; Yuanmei was ordered by urgent relay to Quanzhou, served as acting land commander of Fujian, and was stationed at Hanjiang to coordinate support.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1787 Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan; Yuanmei was rushed to Quanzhou as acting Fujian land commander and stationed at Hanjiang to coordinate the response.

sentences.zh: 至福州，奏言：「師渡台灣，亂民潰散，慮入內山與生番勾結。

translations.literal: On reaching Fuzhou he memorialized: "When the army crosses to Taiwan the rebels will scatter, and I fear they may flee into the inner mountains and join with the raw aborigines.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuzhou he warned: "Once our forces cross to Taiwan the rebels will scatter, and I fear they may flee into the mountains and ally with the aborigines.

sentences.zh: 」上諭令速捕治，俾盡根株。

translations.literal: " The emperor instructed that they be swiftly captured and punished so that the roots might be wholly extirpated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them hunted down quickly so the rebellion could be uprooted entirely.

sentences.zh: 水師提督黃仕簡率兵討爽文，坐逗留奪官，以命元枚，並賜孔雀翎，授參贊，趣率兵渡鹿仔港，會總督常青進討。

translations.literal: The naval commander Huang Shijian had led troops against Shuangwen but was stripped of office for delay; Yuanmei was appointed in his place, granted the peacock feather, made an assistant in the campaign, and urged to lead troops across at Lukang Harbor to join Governor-General Chang Qing in the advance.
translations.idiomatic: Naval Commander Huang Shijian had been dismissed for delay against Shuangwen; Yuanmei replaced him, received the peacock feather, was made campaign assistant, and was ordered to cross at Lukang Harbor and join Governor-General Chang Qing.

sentences.zh: 六月，元枚率兵次鹿仔港，與總兵普吉保師會，即夜，師分道自柴坑仔、大武隴入，殺賊甚眾。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Yuanmei led his troops to Lukang Harbor, joined forces with the commander Pu Jibao, and that same night the army divided, entering by Chaikengzi and Dawulong and killing a great many rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yuanmei reached Lukang Harbor, united with Commander Pu Jibao, and that night split his force through Chaikengzi and Dawulong, killing many rebels.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，賜雙眼孔雀翎。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 元枚所將止浙江兵二千，奏請益師，上命總督李侍堯發福建兵二千、廣東兵三千益元枚。

translations.literal: The troops Yuanmei commanded were only two thousand Zhejiang soldiers; he memorialized requesting reinforcements, and the emperor ordered Governor-General Li Shiyao to send two thousand Fujian troops and three thousand Guangdong troops to augment Yuanmei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmei had only two thousand Zhejiang troops; he asked for reinforcements, and the emperor ordered Li Shiyao to send two thousand Fujian and three thousand Guangdong troops to his aid.

sentences.zh: 時總兵柴大紀堅守諸羅，元枚使告大紀，期會兵攻鬥六門。

translations.literal: At that time the commander Chai Daji was holding Zhuluo firmly; Yuanmei sent word to Daji arranging a rendezvous to attack Douliumen together.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Chai Daji was still holding Zhuluo; Yuanmei sent word arranging a joint attack on Douliumen.

sentences.zh: 戰阿棟社，戰埤頭莊、大肚溪，屢殺賊。

translations.literal: He fought at Adongshe, fought at Pitouzhuang and Dadu Creek, and repeatedly killed rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Adongshe, Pitouzhuang, and Dadu Creek, killing rebels again and again.

sentences.zh: 復進攻西螺，焚條圳塘、中浦厝諸地賊莊。

translations.literal: He again advanced against Xiluo and burned the rebel villages at Tiaozhuntang, Zhongpucuo, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Xiluo and burned rebel villages at Tiaozhuntang, Zhongpucuo, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 元枚族人啟能等七十九人自賊中出，使為導。

translations.literal: Seventy-nine of Yuanmei's clansmen, including Qineng, came out from among the rebels and were made guides.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-nine of Yuanmei's kinsmen, including Qineng, escaped from the rebels and served as guides.

sentences.zh: 元枚奏聞，並言如察出啟能等已從賊，當立誅。

translations.literal: Yuanmei reported this and also said that if investigation showed Qineng and the others had already followed the rebels, they should be executed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmei reported this and added that if Qineng and the others were found to have served the rebels, they should be executed immediately.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其公當，賜緙絲蟒袍、上佩荷包，並諭：「啟能等既來歸，前此已否從賊，不須追詰。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his impartiality, granted him a brocaded python robe and an imperial purse to wear, and instructed: "Since Qineng and the others have now come over, whether they followed the rebels before need not be pursued in inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his fairness, gave him a brocaded python robe and an imperial purse, and said: "Now that Qineng and the others have surrendered, do not investigate whether they had served the rebels before.

sentences.zh: 」諸羅被圍已兩月，大紀屢就告急，上屢趣元枚赴援，諭：「廷珍平硃一貴，七日而事定。

translations.literal: " Zhuluo had been besieged for two months; Daji repeatedly sent urgent appeals, and the emperor repeatedly urged Yuanmei to go to the relief, saying: "Tingzhen pacified Zhu Yigui in seven days and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuluo had been under siege for two months, and Daji's appeals grew desperate; the emperor repeatedly pressed Yuanmei to relieve the city, reminding him: "Tingzhen put down Zhu Yigui in seven days.

sentences.zh: 元枚當效法其祖，毋負委任。

translations.literal: Yuanmei should take his grandfather as his model and not fail the trust placed in him."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmei should follow his grandfather's example and not betray the trust placed in him."

sentences.zh: 」七月，元枚病作。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Yuanmei fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yuanmei fell ill.

sentences.zh: 八月，賊自竹子腳、大肚溪、柴坑仔三道來攻。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the rebels attacked from three routes: Zhuzijiao, Dadu Creek, and Chaikengzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the rebels attacked along three routes—from Zhuzijiao, Dadu Creek, and Chaikengzi.

sentences.zh: 元枚力疾出戰，病益劇，越十日，卒於軍，贈太子太保，發白金千兩治喪，賜祭葬，諡襄毅。

translations.literal: Yuanmei forced himself out to battle despite illness; his sickness grew worse, and ten days later he died in camp. He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; one thousand taels of silver were issued for his funeral, sacrificial burial honors were granted, and he was given the posthumous title Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmei dragged himself into battle despite his illness, which then worsened; ten days later he died in camp. He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given a thousand taels for his funeral and state burial honors, and titled Xiangyi, "Resolute and Steadfast."

sentences.zh: 元枚諡同廷珍，時稱小襄毅以別之。

translations.literal: Yuanmei's posthumous title was the same as Tingzhen's, and at the time he was called "the lesser Xiangyi" to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title matched his grandfather's, and contemporaries called him "the lesser Xiangyi" to distinguish the two.

sentences.zh: 蔡攀龍，福建同安人。

translations.literal: Cai Panlong was a native of Tong'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Panlong came from Tong'an in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 自行伍屢遷至福建澎湖右營游擊。

translations.literal: From the ranks he rose in succession to brigade commander of the right battalion at Penghu in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks to brigade commander of the Penghu right battalion in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十一年，林爽文為亂，巡撫徐嗣曾檄詣軍。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of the Qianlong reign, when Lin Shuangwen rebelled, the provincial governor Xu Sizeng summoned him by dispatch to join the army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1786, when Lin Shuangwen rebelled, Governor Xu Sizeng ordered him to the front.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，賊破鳳山，總兵柴大紀令督兵捕治。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year the rebels took Fengshan, and the commander Chai Daji ordered him to direct troops in pursuit and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In 1787 the rebels took Fengshan, and Commander Chai Daji put him in charge of the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 賊攻台灣府城，攀龍出戰，屢破賊。

translations.literal: When the rebels attacked the Taiwan prefectural city, Panlong went out to fight and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels assaulted the Taiwan prefectural seat, Panlong took the field and beat them back repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 賊屯西園莊，攀龍率諸將瑚圖裡、丁朝雄分道攻之，殺賊三百。

translations.literal: The rebels were encamped at Xiyuanzhuang; Panlong led the commanders Hutuli and Ding Chaoxiong in a divided attack and killed three hundred rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Xiyuanzhuang; Panlong led Hutuli and Ding Chaoxiong in a pincer attack that killed three hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊復攻府城，總督常青令攀龍率諸將孫全謀​​、黃像新等禦戰。

translations.literal: When the rebels again attacked the prefectural city, Governor-General Chang Qing ordered Panlong to lead the commanders Sun Quanmou, Huang Xiangxin, and others in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels assaulted the prefectural seat again, Governor-General Chang Qing ordered Panlong to lead Sun Quanmou, Huang Xiangxin, and others in the defense.

sentences.zh: 賊乘東、南二門，攀龍等力戰，殺賊數百，奪九節砲。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked by the east and south gates; Panlong and others fought fiercely, killed several hundred rebels, and captured a nine-section cannon.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels struck the east and south gates; Panlong and his men fought hard, killed hundreds of rebels, and seized a nine-section cannon.

sentences.zh: 論功，擢北路協副將，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to deputy commander of the northern route and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to deputy commander of the northern route and given the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 賊復至，攀龍督戰，复殺賊三百餘，予強勝巴圖魯名號。

translations.literal: When the rebels came again, Panlong directed the fighting and again killed more than three hundred; he was given the title of Strong Victor Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels returned, Panlong led the fight and killed another three hundred; he received the title Strong Victor Baturu.

sentences.zh: 七月，常青令攀龍援柴大紀諸羅，上命授海壇鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Chang Qing ordered Panlong to relieve Chai Daji at Zhuluo; the emperor appointed him garrison commander at Haitan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Chang Qing sent Panlong to relieve Chai Daji at Zhuluo, and the emperor made him Haitan garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 攀龍師至鹽水港，分八隊以進。

translations.literal: Panlong's army reached Yanshui Harbor and advanced in eight columns.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong reached Yanshui Harbor and advanced in eight columns.

sentences.zh: 雨大至，賊乘雨合圍，諸將貴林、楊起麟、杭富皆戰死。

translations.literal: Heavy rain fell; the rebels used the rain to surround them, and the commanders Guilin, Yang Qilin, and Hang Fu all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: A downpour came; the rebels used the rain to surround them, and commanders Guilin, Yang Qilin, and Hang Fu were all killed.

sentences.zh: 會大紀以師來迎，攀龍及全謀兵不及千人，偕運餉民三千人入諸羅，復出城殺賊。

translations.literal: Daji came out with troops to meet them; Panlong and Sun Quanmou had fewer than a thousand soldiers; together with three thousand grain porters they entered Zhuluo and again went out of the city to kill rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Daji met them with troops; Panlong and Sun Quanmou had fewer than a thousand men; with three thousand supply porters they entered Zhuluo and sallied out again to strike the rebels.

sentences.zh: 總督李侍堯聞攀龍兵達諸羅，未知貴林等戰死狀，謂諸羅圍已解，入告。

translations.literal: Governor-General Li Shiyao heard that Panlong's troops had reached Zhuluo and, not knowing that Guilin and the others had died in battle, reported that the siege of Zhuluo was already lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Li Shiyao heard Panlong had reached Zhuluo and, unaware that Guilin and the others had been killed, reported the siege lifted.

sentences.zh: 上擢攀龍陸路提督，參贊軍務，貴林、起麟、全謀並遷官。

translations.literal: The emperor promoted Panlong to land commander, made him an assistant in military affairs, and advanced Guilin, Qilin, and Quanmou in rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promoted Panlong to land commander and campaign assistant, and advanced Guilin, Qilin, and Quanmou.

sentences.zh: 俄，侍堯复疏陳，上命卹戰死諸將。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Shiyao sent a further memorial clarifying the matter, and the emperor ordered compensation for the commanders who had died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shiyao sent a corrective memorial, and the emperor ordered pensions for the fallen commanders.

sentences.zh: 福康安既解嘉義圍，疏劾大紀，因言攀龍軍嘉義西門外，並無出城殺賊事，自請奪職。

translations.literal: After Fuk'anggan had lifted the siege of Jiayi, he memorialized impeaching Daji and also said that Panlong's army had been outside the west gate of Jiayi and that there had been no affair of going out of the city to kill rebels; Panlong asked that his office be stripped.
translations.idiomatic: After Fuk'anggan relieved Jiayi, he impeached Daji and noted that Panlong's troops had camped outside Jiayi's west gate with no record of sallying out to kill rebels; Panlong asked to be stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 擬請令還海壇本任。

translations.literal: It was proposed that he be ordered back to his original post at Haitan.
translations.idiomatic: The court proposed sending him back to his Haitan post.

sentences.zh: 上謂攀龍屢戰有功，其過尚可寬。

translations.literal: The emperor said that Panlong had repeatedly fought with merit and that his fault could still be leniently treated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said Panlong had fought well repeatedly and his fault could be overlooked.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，逮大紀治罪，移攀龍水師提督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year Daji was arrested for punishment, and Panlong was transferred to naval commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1788 Daji was arrested for trial, and Panlong was made naval commander.

sentences.zh: 師攻大武隴，令攀龍駐灣里溪。

translations.literal: As the army attacked Dawulong, Panlong was ordered to hold Wanlixi.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Dawulong, Panlong was stationed at Wanlixi.

sentences.zh: 爽文既擒，其弟勇及賊渠莊大田猶窺伺府城，攻灣里溪，圖斷府城道。

translations.literal: After Shuangwen was captured, his younger brother Yong and the rebel chieftain Zhuang Datian still watched the prefectural city, attacked Wanlixi, and sought to cut the road to the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuangwen's capture, his brother Yong and rebel chief Zhuang Datian still menaced the prefectural seat, attacked Wanlixi, and tried to sever its supply route.

sentences.zh: 福康安遣攀龍分道進攻，頗有斬獲。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan sent Panlong to attack along separate routes, with considerable kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan sent Panlong on divided attacks that yielded many kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 事平，圖形紫光閣，列前二十功臣，上自為贊，許為台灣戰將中巨擘。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor among the first twenty meritorious subjects; the emperor himself composed the encomium and acknowledged him as a leading figure among Taiwan's battle commanders.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion ended his portrait joined the Hall of Purple Splendor's top twenty heroes; the emperor wrote his encomium himself and hailed him as the greatest of Taiwan's battlefield generals.

sentences.zh: 師還，諸將言攀龍平庸，福康安亦言未能勝任，左遷江南狼山鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the commanders said Panlong was mediocre; Fuk'anggan also said he could not fill the post, and he was demoted to garrison commander at Langshan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: After the army withdrew, other generals called Panlong mediocre; Fuk'anggan agreed he was unfit for high command, and he was demoted to Langshan garrison commander in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Jiaqing reign he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1798.

sentences.zh: 梁朝桂，甘肅中衛人。

translations.literal: Liang Chaogui was a native of Zhongwei in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chaogui came from Zhongwei in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年，以中衛營外委從征金川，先後攻克路頂宗、布朗郭宗及功噶爾拉、丫口、昔嶺、阿喀木雅。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of the Qianlong reign, as an external agent of the Zhongwei garrison he followed the campaign against Jinchuan and in succession captured Ludingzong, Bulangguozong, Gongga'erla, Yakou, Xiling, and Akemuya.
translations.idiomatic: In 1772, as a Zhongwei garrison agent, he joined the Jinchuan campaign and took Ludingzong, Bulangguozong, Gongga'erla, Yakou, Xiling, and Akemuya in turn.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，克淜普，進攻喇穆喇穆山梁，奪日丫口。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he took Qinpu, advanced against the Lamulamu ridge, and seized Riyakou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1774 he captured Qinpu, assaulted the Lamulamu ridge, and took Riyakou.

sentences.zh: 四十年，剿勒吉爾博寨，先登被創。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he suppressed the Leji'erbo stockade, was first to scale the wall, and was wounded.
translations.idiomatic: In 1775 he stormed the Leji'erbo stockade, was first over the wall, and was wounded.

sentences.zh: 四月，攻木思工噶克山，潛師入，盡克其城碉，據康薩爾至丫口山。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he attacked Musigonggake Mountain; troops entered secretly and wholly captured its walled towers and blockhouses, holding the ground from Kangsar to Yakoushan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he attacked Musigonggake Mountain with a stealth column, captured all its fortifications, and held the line from Kangsar to Yakoushan.

sentences.zh: 十月，克西里山。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he took Xilishan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he captured Xilishan.

sentences.zh: 錄功，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: His merits were recorded and he received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 累遷陝西潼關協副將。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to deputy commander of the Tongguan command in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy commander of the Tongguan command in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 金川平，列五十功臣，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: When Jinchuan was pacified he was listed among the fifty meritorious subjects and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinchuan was pacified he ranked among the fifty heroes and his portrait entered the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 累遷甘肅肅州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to garrison commander at Suzhou in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He became garrison commander at Suzhou in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 坐事罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 復起，自福建福寧鎮移廣東高廉鎮。

translations.literal: He was restored to office, moved from the Funing garrison in Fujian to the Gaolian garrison in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed, moving from Funing in Fujian to Gaolian in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，台灣林爽文為亂，莊大田應之，別為南路賊。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan; Zhuang Datian responded to him and formed a separate southern-route rebel force.
translations.idiomatic: In 1787 Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan; Zhuang Datian joined him and led a separate southern rebel force.

sentences.zh: 朝桂率兵敗大田於蔦松，斬馘二百餘。

translations.literal: Chaogui led troops and defeated Datian at Niaosong, taking more than two hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Chaogui defeated Datian at Niaosong, killing more than two hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊眾數千犯大營，擊卻之，斃賊三百。

translations.literal: Several thousand rebels attacked the main camp; he beat them back and killed three hundred rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When several thousand rebels assaulted the main camp, he drove them off and killed three hundred.

sentences.zh: 將軍常青慮南路賊北擾諸羅，檄朝桂堵禦，連敗之南潭、中洲、十三里莊，殲數百人。

translations.literal: General Chang Qing feared the southern rebels would move north to trouble Zhuluo and ordered Chaogui to block them; he repeatedly defeated them at Nantan, Zhongzhou, and Shisanlizhuang and destroyed several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing southern rebels would threaten Zhuluo from the north, Chang Qing ordered Chaogui to hold them; he beat them repeatedly at Nantan, Zhongzhou, and Shisanlizhuang, killing hundreds.

sentences.zh: 九月，常青移師北路剿爽文，以朝桂守台灣府城，賊來犯，擊走之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Chang Qing shifted his army to the northern route to suppress Shuangwen and left Chaogui to guard the Taiwan prefectural city; when rebels came to attack, Chaogui drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Chang Qing marched north against Shuangwen and left Chaogui to defend the Taiwan prefectural seat; when rebels attacked, Chaogui repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 其冬，援參贊恆瑞於鹽水港，毀賊藔，賜號奮勇巴圖魯；

translations.literal: That winter he went to reinforce the assistant Heng Rui at Yanshui Harbor, destroyed rebel huts, and was granted the title Valiant Baturu;
translations.idiomatic: That winter he reinforced Assistant Commander Heng Rui at Yanshui Harbor, burned rebel huts, and received the title Valiant Baturu;

sentences.zh: 復同恆瑞自鹿仔草進剿鎮平莊，受創，力戰敗賊。

translations.literal: he again joined Heng Rui in advancing from Luzicao to suppress Zhenpingzhuang, was wounded, and fought fiercely to defeat the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: he joined Heng Rui again in an advance from Luzicao on Zhenpingzhuang, was wounded, and fought through to defeat the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時提督柴大紀被圍諸羅急，朝桂欲馳援，恆瑞不聽，大紀以聞，帝令將軍福康安察奏。

translations.literal: At that time Commander-in-Chief Chai Daji was urgently besieged at Zhuluo; Chaogui wished to ride to the relief, but Heng Rui would not listen; Daji reported this, and the emperor ordered General Fuk'anggan to investigate and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief Chai Daji was desperately besieged at Zhuluo; Chaogui wanted to relieve him, but Heng Rui refused; Daji reported this, and the emperor ordered Fuk'anggan to investigate.

sentences.zh: 會福康安抵鹿仔港，檄朝桂仍駐守鹽水港及鹿仔草。

translations.literal: When Fuk'anggan reached Lukang Harbor he ordered Chaogui to remain on guard at Yanshui Harbor and Luzicao.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuk'anggan reached Lukang Harbor he ordered Chaogui to hold Yanshui Harbor and Luzicao.

sentences.zh: 五十三年春，就擢福建陸路提督。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifty-third year he was promoted on the spot to land commander of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1788 he was promoted to Fujian land commander.

sentences.zh: 檄剿麻豆莊、大武隴屯賊，通郡城要道。

translations.literal: He was ordered to suppress the rebels at Madouzhuang and the Dawulong garrison and open the vital route to the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to clear rebels from Madouzhuang and the Dawulong garrison and reopen the route to the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 大田時據大武隴拒守，朝桂自茅港尾繞至阿里港迎截；

translations.literal: Datian was then holding Dawulong in defense; Chaogui circled from Maogangwei to Ali Harbor to intercept him;
translations.idiomatic: Datian was holding Dawulong; Chaogui swung from Maogangwei to Ali Harbor to cut him off;

sentences.zh: 复赴打狗、竹仔各港口截其走路。

translations.literal: he again went to the ports of Dagou and Zhuzai to cut off his escape routes.
translations.idiomatic: he also blocked escape routes at the ports of Dagou and Zhuzai.

sentences.zh: 大田力不支，自牛莊竄極南之郎嶠，負山阻海。

translations.literal: Datian could not hold out, fled from Niuzhuang to Langqiao at the far south, and relied on mountains to block the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Overmatched, Datian fled from Niuzhuang to remote Langqiao in the far south, backed against mountains and sea.

sentences.zh: 福康安自風港進至柴城，分六隊直逼海岸，與朝桂環攻之，大田及他賊目四十餘悉就擒。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan advanced from Fenggang to Chaicheng, divided six columns to press straight to the coast, and with Chaogui surrounded and attacked them; Datian and more than forty other rebel leaders were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan advanced from Fenggang to Chaicheng, sent six columns to the coast, and with Chaogui encircled them; Datian and more than forty rebel chiefs were captured.

sentences.zh: 台灣平，再圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: When Taiwan was pacified his portrait was again placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwan was pacified his portrait again entered the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 金門巡洋艦被劫，以朝桂不能戢盜，移廣西。

translations.literal: A Kinmen patrol vessel was seized by pirates; because Chaogui could not restrain bandits he was transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When a Kinmen patrol ship was seized by pirates, Chaogui was blamed for failing to control banditry and transferred to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 再移湖廣。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 普吉保，札庫塔氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Pu Jibao, of the Zhakuta clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Jibao, of the Zhakuta clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十年，以藍翎侍衛從軍徵烏什，有功，補三等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of the Qianlong reign, as a bodyguard with the blue feather he followed the army in the campaign against Ushi, performed merit, and was appointed a third-rank bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1765, as a blue-feather guardsman, he joined the campaign against Ushi, distinguished himself, and was made a third-rank guardsman.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，從參贊大臣舒常攻日旁，有功。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he followed the assistant grand minister Shu Chang in attacking Ripang and performed merit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1772 he followed Assistant Minister Shu Chang against Ripang and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，從副將軍豐升額攻凱立葉山，進抵迪噶拉穆札山。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he followed the deputy general Feng Sheng'e in attacking Kailiye Mountain and advanced to Digalamuzha Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In 1774 he followed Deputy General Feng Sheng'e against Kailiye Mountain and reached Digalamuzha Mountain.

sentences.zh: 賊分三隊，普吉保偕侍衛瑪爾占等夾攻，斃賊無算，賜衝捷巴圖魯名號。

translations.literal: The rebels divided into three columns; Pu Jibao together with the bodyguard Ma'erzhan and others attacked from both sides and killed rebels beyond counting; he was granted the title Swift Assault Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels split into three columns; Pu Jibao and Guardsman Ma'erzhan attacked from both flanks and killed countless rebels; he received the title Swift Assault Baturu.

sentences.zh: 四十年，攻噶爾丹寺諸地，連破木城、石碉。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he attacked the regions of Galdan Temple and in succession broke wooden walls and stone blockhouses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1775 he attacked the Galdan Temple region and stormed wooden walls and stone blockhouses in succession.

sentences.zh: 上獎普吉保勇往，累擢福建汀州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Pu Jibao's bold advance and promoted him in succession to garrison commander at Tingzhou in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his boldness and promoted him to Tingzhou garrison commander in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 林爽文為亂，總督常青檄普吉保會剿，五十二年，率水師渡台灣，迭破賊鹿仔港、八卦山，上嘉其奮勉。

translations.literal: When Lin Shuangwen rebelled, Governor-General Chang Qing summoned Pu Jibao to join in suppression; in the fifty-second year he led the naval force across to Taiwan, repeatedly defeated the rebels at Lukang Harbor and Baguashan, and the emperor praised his energetic effort.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Shuangwen rebelled, Chang Qing summoned Pu Jibao to the campaign; in 1787 he led the navy to Taiwan, took Lukang Harbor and Baguashan in succession, and won the emperor's praise for his vigor.

sentences.zh: 爽文見師至，退守鬥六門、大里杙。

translations.literal: When Shuangwen saw the army arrive he withdrew to hold Douliumen and Dali.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the army arrive, Shuangwen withdrew to Douliumen and Dali.

sentences.zh: 普吉保以師進，爽文攻諸羅，赴援，抵笨港，率游擊海亮等殲賊數百，毀賊莊七，得旨嘉獎，賜玉搬指、荷包、蟒袍。

translations.literal: Pu Jibao advanced with his army; Shuangwen attacked Zhuluo, and he went to the relief, reaching Bengang; he led the brigade commander Hailiang and others in destroying several hundred rebels and seven rebel villages; he received an edict of praise and was granted a jade thumb ring, purse, and python robe.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Jibao advanced; when Shuangwen besieged Zhuluo he marched to relieve the city, reached Bengang, and with Brigade Commander Hailiang destroyed hundreds of rebels and seven rebel villages; the emperor commended him and gave him a jade thumb ring, purse, and python robe.

sentences.zh: 笨港潰賊糾眾截我兵，普吉保擊斬甚眾。

translations.literal: Routed rebels at Bengang gathered a crowd to intercept our troops; Pu Jibao struck and killed a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Routed rebels at Bengang rallied to ambush government troops; Pu Jibao killed many of them.

sentences.zh: 嗣以駐兵元長莊、月眉莊不進，旨嚴飭。

translations.literal: Later, because he held his troops at Yuanchangzhuang and Yuemeizhuang without advancing, an edict sternly rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was sternly rebuked for camping at Yuanchangzhuang and Yuemeizhuang without advancing.

sentences.zh: 尋攻大埔林，收復鬥六門。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he attacked Dapulin and recovered Douliumen.
translations.idiomatic: He soon attacked Dapulin and recovered Douliumen.

sentences.zh: 爽文竄內山，普吉保從諸將徒步陟山搜捕。

translations.literal: Shuangwen fled into the inner mountains; Pu Jibao followed the other commanders on foot up the mountains in search and capture.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen fled into the mountains; Pu Jibao joined the other generals in climbing on foot to hunt him down.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，以兵扼科仔坑口，合圍，俘爽文。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, with troops blocking Kezikengkou, he joined in surrounding Shuangwen and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1788 his troops sealed Kezikengkou, joined the encirclement, and captured Shuangwen.

sentences.zh: 南路莊大田亦就擒。

translations.literal: Zhuang Datian on the southern route was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: The southern rebel chief Zhuang Datian was captured as well.

sentences.zh: 台灣平，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: When Taiwan was pacified his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwan was pacified his portrait entered the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 普吉保初克鹿仔港，以福康安疏薦，授台灣總兵。

translations.literal: When Pu Jibao first took Lukang Harbor, Fuk'anggan memorialized recommending him, and he was appointed garrison commander of Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: After Pu Jibao first took Lukang Harbor, Fuk'anggan recommended him and he was made Taiwan garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 明年，上念台灣初定，慮普吉保不能勝，命解任。

translations.literal: The next year, considering that Taiwan had only just been settled and fearing that Pu Jibao could not fill the post, the emperor ordered him relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, fearing Pu Jibao was unequal to governing newly pacified Taiwan, the emperor removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 尋授廣西左江鎮，坐責把總黎振乾投水死，戍伊犁。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed to the Zuojiang garrison in Guangxi; because a corporal under his command, Li Zhenqian, drowned himself he was banished to garrison duty at Yili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed to the Zuojiang garrison in Guangxi, but when a corporal under his command drowned himself he was exiled to Yili.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 丁朝雄，字伯宜，江蘇通州人。

translations.literal: Ding Chaoxiong, style Boyi, was a native of Tongzhou in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Chaoxiong, styled Boyi, came from Tongzhou in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 自行伍累擢福建台灣水師副將。

translations.literal: From the ranks he rose in succession to deputy commander of the Taiwan naval force in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks to deputy commander of the Taiwan naval force in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十一年，以任滿赴部引見，至省城，聞林爽文亂起。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of the Qianlong reign, when his term ended he went to the ministry for audience on departure; reaching the provincial capital he heard that Lin Shuangwen's rebellion had broken out.
translations.idiomatic: In 1786, at the end of his term, he went to the capital for audience; at the provincial seat he learned Lin Shuangwen had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 朝雄策東港與鳳山犄角，爽文所必爭，白總督常青，請兵屯東港，斷其糧道。

translations.literal: Chaoxiong proposed that Donggang and Fengshan stood in mutual support like horn and corner and were ground Shuangwen was sure to contest; he informed Governor-General Chang Qing and asked for troops to hold Donggang and cut the grain route.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoxiong argued that Donggang and Fengshan formed a strategic pair Shuangwen was bound to contest, told Chang Qing, and asked for troops at Donggang to sever rebel supplies.

sentences.zh: 常青不能用，遣朝雄還台灣，佐海壇鎮總兵郝壯猷討爽文。

translations.literal: Chang Qing could not adopt the plan and sent Chaoxiong back to Taiwan to assist Haitan garrison commander Hao Zhuangyou in suppressing Shuangwen.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Qing rejected the plan and sent Chaoxiong back to Taiwan to assist Haitan Garrison Commander Hao Zhuangyou against Shuangwen.

sentences.zh: 五十二年春，壯猷偕朝雄率兵二千餘擊賊，馘三百，俘二十五。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifty-second year Zhuangyou together with Chaoxiong led more than two thousand troops against the rebels, took three hundred heads, and captured twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1787 Zhuangyou and Chaoxiong led more than two thousand men against the rebels, killing three hundred and capturing twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 日將暮，賊復來攻，朝雄复殺賊百餘，賊始去。

translations.literal: As day was nearing dusk the rebels attacked again; Chaoxiong again killed more than a hundred, and the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the rebels attacked again; Chaoxiong killed another hundred and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 攻鳳山，朝雄乘東門，首諸軍入，鳳山遂復。

translations.literal: In the attack on Fengshan, Chaoxiong took the east gate and was first of the armies to enter; Fengshan was thus recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Fengshan, Chaoxiong took the east gate and led the army in; Fengshan was recovered.

sentences.zh: 黃仕簡檄朝雄守安平海口。

translations.literal: Huang Shijian ordered Chaoxiong by dispatch to guard the Anping sea mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shijian ordered Chaoxiong to guard the Anping harbor mouth.

sentences.zh: 賊攻府城，朝雄偕知府楊廷樺督兵民力禦。

translations.literal: When the rebels attacked the prefectural city, Chaoxiong together with the prefect Yang Tinghua directed soldiers and civilians in strenuous defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels assaulted the prefectural seat, Chaoxiong and Prefect Yang Tinghua led troops and militia in a hard defense.

sentences.zh: 賊攻桶盤棧，朝雄為前鋒，出戰，台灣道永福、同知楊廷理率兵民繼，复殺賊百餘，賊敗走。

translations.literal: When the rebels attacked Tongpan Stockade, Chaoxiong served as vanguard and went out to fight; the Taiwan intendant Yongfu and the subprefect Yang Tingli led soldiers and civilians after him; they again killed more than a hundred rebels and the rebels were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels attacked Tongpan Stockade, Chaoxiong led the vanguard; Intendant Yongfu and Subprefect Yang Tingli followed with troops and militia; they killed another hundred rebels and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 冬，朝雄偕游擊倪賓率兵千二百、義民二千餘攻東港。

translations.literal: In winter Chaoxiong together with the brigade commander Ni Bin led twelve hundred troops and more than two thousand militia in an attack on Donggang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Chaoxiong and Brigade Commander Ni Bin led twelve hundred troops and more than two thousand militiamen against Donggang.

sentences.zh: 東港賊數万，其渠吳豹以海岸淺，度舟不能至，不為備。

translations.literal: At Donggang the rebels numbered tens of thousands; their chieftain Wu Bao, judging the coast shallow and expecting that boats could not reach it, made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of rebels held Donggang; their chief Wu Bao, thinking the shallow coast would keep boats away, made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 朝雄遣諜以水注賊砲，乘雨至水漲，遣兵民分道登岸殺賊，俘豹。

translations.literal: Chaoxiong sent spies to pour water into the rebel cannon; taking advantage of rain until the water rose, he sent soldiers and civilians ashore by separate routes to kill rebels and captured Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoxiong sent agents to flood the rebel guns with water; when rain raised the water level he landed troops and militia along several routes, killed rebels, and captured Bao.

sentences.zh: 以兵寡不能克，報常青請益兵。

translations.literal: Because his troops were too few to overcome them, he reported to Chang Qing requesting reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Too few to finish the job, he asked Chang Qing for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 常青令駐港口護餉道。

translations.literal: Chang Qing ordered him to remain at the harbor to protect the grain route.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Qing ordered him to hold the harbor and protect the supply line.

sentences.zh: 既，令攻竹仔港，毀賊舟。

translations.literal: Later he was ordered to attack Zhuzai Harbor and destroy rebel boats.
translations.idiomatic: He was later ordered to attack Zhuzai Harbor and destroy rebel boats.

sentences.zh: 五十三年春，復攻東港，仍遣諜以水注賊砲，督兵攻渡口，賊驚竄，逐三十餘裡，乃倚山而軍。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifty-third year he again attacked Donggang, again sent spies to pour water into the rebel cannon, directed troops against the crossing, the rebels fled in alarm, were pursued more than thirty li, and then encamped leaning on the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1788 he attacked Donggang again, again flooded the rebel guns, stormed the crossing, routed the rebels for more than thirty li, and encamped against the hills.

sentences.zh: 賊夜來犯，朝雄戒勿動；

translations.literal: The rebels came to attack by night; Chaoxiong ordered that they must not move;
translations.idiomatic: Rebels attacked by night; Chaoxiong ordered his men to hold still;

sentences.zh: 及曉，賊倦，掩擊，大破之。

translations.literal: when dawn came the rebels were weary; he struck from ambush and broke them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: at dawn, when the rebels were exhausted, he struck from ambush and routed them.

sentences.zh: 爽文遣其徒來援，朝雄築壘困之。

translations.literal: Shuangwen sent his followers to relieve them; Chaoxiong built stockades to hem them in.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen sent reinforcements; Chaoxiong built stockades to trap them.

sentences.zh: 賊潰圍出，設伏斷其歸路，而自將追之，大破賊，遂復東港。

translations.literal: The rebels broke out of the encirclement; he set an ambush to cut off their return route and himself led the pursuit, utterly defeating the rebels, and thus recovered Donggang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke out; he ambushed their retreat while leading the pursuit himself, crushed them, and recovered Donggang.

sentences.zh: 福康安上其功，授海壇鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan reported his merit, and he was appointed garrison commander at Haitan.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan reported his merits, and he was made Haitan garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 既，福康安劾柴大紀受陋規，言朝雄為安平協副將時亦有此，當奪職戍軍台，上以朝雄攻東港戰有功，命留任。

translations.literal: Later Fuk'anggan impeached Chai Daji for accepting petty bribes and said that when Chaoxiong had been deputy commander of the Anping command he had done the same and ought to be stripped of office and banished to the military garrison; the emperor, considering Chaoxiong's merit in fighting at Donggang, ordered him retained in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fuk'anggan impeached Chai Daji for taking petty bribes and said Chaoxiong had done the same as Anping deputy commander and should be stripped and exiled; the emperor kept him in office for his merits at Donggang.

sentences.zh: 林鬎舵、林明灼者，海盜渠也，五十四年，朝雄巡洋至汜澳，破盜巢，得鬎舵等；

translations.literal: Lin Huduo and Lin Mingzhuo were pirate chieftains; in the fifty-fourth year Chaoxiong on patrol reached Xiao'ao, broke their nest, and captured Huduo and others;
translations.idiomatic: Pirate chiefs Lin Huduo and Lin Mingzhuo were active in 1789 when Chaoxiong on patrol reached Xiao'ao, destroyed their base, and captured Huduo;

sentences.zh: 而明灼拒殺參將張殿魁。

translations.literal: but Mingzhuo resisted and killed the deputy commander Zhang Diankui.
translations.idiomatic: but Mingzhuo resisted and killed Deputy Commander Zhang Diankui.

sentences.zh: 上責總督伍拉納，伍拉納以屬朝雄，督舟師出海，遇諸大麥洋，俟其近，發大砲，斃數酋，明灼窮蹙，躍入海，官軍鉤致，俘以歸。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Governor-General Wulana; Wulana assigned the matter to Chaoxiong, who directed the fleet to sea; at Zhudamaiyang they waited until the enemy drew near, fired great cannon, killed several chieftains; Mingzhuo, hard pressed, leaped into the sea; government troops hooked him up and brought him back captive.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Governor-General Wulana, who put Chaoxiong in charge; Chaoxiong took the fleet to Zhudamaiyang, waited until the pirates closed, opened fire with heavy guns, and killed several chiefs; cornered, Mingzhuo leaped into the sea, was hooked up by government troops, and brought back captive.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，追論朝雄在台灣失察天地會邪教，當奪職；

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year he was retrospectively judged for failing to detect the Heaven and Earth Society heterodox cult in Taiwan and ought to have been stripped of office;
translations.idiomatic: In 1790 he was retrospectively blamed for failing to detect the Heaven and Earth Society in Taiwan and was to be stripped of office;

sentences.zh: 上諮伍拉納朝雄在官狀，伍拉納言朝雄督水師捕盜有勞，命還任。

translations.literal: The emperor consulted Wulana about Chaoxiong's official conduct; Wulana said Chaoxiong had merit in directing the navy to capture pirates and he was ordered back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Wulana about Chaoxiong's conduct; Wulana said he had merit hunting pirates and ordered him restored to office.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，攝水師提督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he served as acting naval commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1793 he served as acting naval commander.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，入覲，至清江浦，病篤。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he went to audience; reaching Qingjiangpu his illness grew critical.
translations.idiomatic: In 1794, on his way to audience, he fell gravely ill at Qingjiangpu.

sentences.zh: 乞罷歸，卒於上海舟中。

translations.literal: He begged to resign and return home and died in his boat at Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to resign and return home, and died aboard his boat at Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 鄂輝，碧魯氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: E Hui, of the Bilu clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: E Hui, of the Bilu clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 自前鋒分發四川試用守備。

translations.literal: From the vanguard corps he was assigned to Sichuan as a probationary garrison commandant.
translations.idiomatic: From the vanguard he was posted to Sichuan as a probationary garrison commandant.

sentences.zh: 七遷建昌鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Through seven promotions he became garrison commander at Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: After seven promotions he became Jianchang garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 從大學士阿桂定蘭州回亂，予法什尚阿巴圖魯名號。

translations.literal: He followed Grand Secretary Agui in pacifying the Muslim rebellion around Lanzhou and was granted the title Fashishang'a Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand Secretary Agui in suppressing the Lanzhou Muslim rebellion and received the title Fashishang'a Baturu.

sentences.zh: 再遷成都將軍。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to general at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Chengdu general.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十二年，署四川總督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of the Qianlong reign he served as acting governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1787 he served as acting governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 將軍福康安討台灣亂民林爽文，上命鄂輝率四川屯練降番濟師。

translations.literal: General Fuk'anggan was suppressing the Taiwan rebel Lin Shuangwen; the emperor ordered E Hui to lead Sichuan garrison militia and surrendered aborigines to reinforce the army.
translations.idiomatic: When General Fuk'anggan campaigned against Lin Shuangwen in Taiwan, the emperor ordered E Hui to lead Sichuan militia and surrendered tribesmen as reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 尋授參贊，從渡海援嘉義。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed campaign assistant and crossed the sea to relieve Jiayi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made campaign assistant and crossed the strait to relieve Jiayi.

sentences.zh: 鄂輝屯東莊溪橋，攻克牛稠山竹柵，嘉義圍解。

translations.literal: E Hui encamped at Dongzhuangxi Bridge, captured the bamboo stockade at Niuchoushan, and the siege of Jiayi was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: E Hui held Dongzhuangxi Bridge, took the Niuchoushan bamboo stockade, and lifted the siege of Jiayi.

sentences.zh: 逐賊至大排竹，殲之。

translations.literal: He pursued the rebels to Dapaizhu and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the rebels to Dapaizhu and annihilated them.

sentences.zh: 師攻鬥六門，賊自山下撲，鄂輝督兵衝截，賊奔逸，攻克大埔林、大埔尾二莊，賊潰。

translations.literal: As the army attacked Douliumen the rebels rushed down from the hills; E Hui directed troops in a charging interception, the rebels fled in disorder, and Dapulin and Dapuwei were taken; the rebels collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Douliumen rebels rushed down from the hills; E Hui led a countercharge, routed them, captured Dapulin and Dapuwei, and broke the rebel force.

sentences.zh: 爽文自所居大里杙奔內山番界，鄂輝逐之至集埔。

translations.literal: Shuangwen fled from his dwelling at Dali into the inner aboriginal borderlands; E Hui pursued him to Jipu.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen fled from Dali into the aboriginal mountains; E Hui pursued him to Jipu.

sentences.zh: 五十三年春，诇知爽文所匿地曰東勢角，福康安督鄂輝及舒亮追捕，自歸仔頭至麻著社，分軍，鄂輝自撲仔離東山路進，舒亮直取東勢角。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifty-third year spies learned that Shuangwen was hiding at a place called Dongshijiao; Fuk'anggan directed E Hui and Shu Liang in pursuit; from Guizaitou to Mazheshe the army divided: E Hui advanced by the eastern route from Puzaili, and Shu Liang went straight for Dongshijiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1788 scouts found Shuangwen hiding at Dongshijiao; Fuk'anggan sent E Hui and Shu Liang after him; from Guizaitou to Mazheshe they split forces—E Hui took the eastern route from Puzaili while Shu Liang struck Dongshijiao directly.

sentences.zh: 是役遂俘爽文，亂乃定。

translations.literal: In this campaign Shuangwen was captured and the rebellion was settled.
translations.idiomatic: In that campaign Shuangwen was captured and the rebellion ended.

sentences.zh: 上命台灣嘉義立諸將帥生祠，鄂輝與焉。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered living shrines to the commanders erected at Jiayi in Taiwan; E Hui was among them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered living shrines to the generals built at Jiayi in Taiwan; E Hui was included.

sentences.zh: 師還，圖形紫光閣，賜雙眼孔雀翎、雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: When the army returned his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor; he was granted the double-eyed peacock feather and the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
translations.idiomatic: After the army withdrew his portrait entered the Hall of Purple Splendor; he received the double-eyed peacock feather and the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.

sentences.zh: 鄂輝朝熱河行在。

translations.literal: E Hui attended the emperor at the Rehe traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: E Hui attended the emperor at the Rehe traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 廓爾喀侵西藏，據濟嚨、聶拉木諸地。

translations.literal: Gurkhas invaded Tibet and occupied Jilong, Nyalam, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: The Gurkhas invaded Tibet and seized Jilong, Nyalam, and other territories.

sentences.zh: 上促鄂輝還四川，與提督成德帥師赴援，又命侍郎巴忠往按。

translations.literal: The emperor urged E Hui to return to Sichuan; together with Commander Cheng De he led troops to the relief, and Vice Minister Ba Zhong was also ordered to go and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed E Hui to return to Sichuan; he and Commander Cheng De led troops to relieve Tibet, and Vice Minister Ba Zhong was sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 巴忠先嘗為駐藏大臣，習藏事，示意噶布倫，令賂廓爾喀返侵地。

translations.literal: Ba Zhong had formerly served as resident minister in Tibet and was versed in Tibetan affairs; he signaled the kaloons to bribe the Gurkhas to return the invaded territory.
translations.idiomatic: Ba Zhong, a former Tibetan resident minister, instructed the kaloons to bribe the Gurkhas into returning the seized lands.

sentences.zh: 鄂輝等遂與議和，疏陳善後事。

translations.literal: E Hui and the others then negotiated peace and memorialized on postwar settlement.
translations.idiomatic: E Hui and his colleagues then made peace and memorialized on the aftermath.

sentences.zh: 尋授四川總督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，廓爾喀渝盟，复侵濟嚨、聶拉木諸地。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year the Gurkhas broke the treaty and again invaded Jilong, Nyalam, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In 1791 the Gurkhas broke the treaty and again invaded Jilong, Nyalam, and neighboring areas.

sentences.zh: 上命將軍福康安督師討廓爾喀，責鄂輝誤用巴忠議致復生事，奪官，予副都統銜駐藏，聽福康安指揮，福康安令督餉。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered General Fuk'anggan to command the expedition against the Gurkhas, blamed E Hui for wrongly adopting Ba Zhong's plan and causing the trouble to recur, stripped his office, gave him the rank of vice commander-in-chief to remain in Tibet under Fuk'anggan's direction, and Fuk'anggan put him in charge of supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent General Fuk'anggan against the Gurkhas, blamed E Hui for following Ba Zhong's bribe scheme and letting the crisis recur, stripped his rank, sent him to Tibet as vice commander under Fuk'anggan, and put him in charge of supplies.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書和琳劾鄂輝得廓爾喀貢表不以上聞，命奪副都統銜，逮赴前藏荷校示罰。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Helin impeached E Hui for receiving Gurkha tribute memorials without reporting them upward; he was ordered stripped of the vice commander's rank, arrested, sent to front Tibet, and made to wear the cangue as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Helin impeached E Hui for concealing Gurkha tribute memorials; he was stripped of vice commander rank, arrested, sent to front Tibet, and punished with the cangue.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，命還京師，授拜唐阿。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he was ordered back to the capital and appointed a baitangga.
translations.idiomatic: In 1793 he was recalled to the capital and appointed a baitangga attendant.

sentences.zh: 加員外郎銜，遷熱河總管。

translations.literal: He was given the rank of vice director and transferred to superintendent of Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: He received vice-director rank and became superintendent of Rehe.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，命以侍衛詣荊州從剿教匪，戰有功，以都統銜加太子少保，授湖南提督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiaqing reign he was ordered as a bodyguard to Jingzhou to join in suppressing the sect rebels; he fought with merit, was given the rank of commander-in-chief with Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and appointed commander of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiaqing reign he was sent as a guardsman to Jingzhou against the White Lotus rebels, distinguished himself, was made commander-in-chief with Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and appointed Hunan commander.

sentences.zh: 屢破賊，與額勒登保等攻克石隆山，斬賊渠石柳鄧，封三等男。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated the rebels; together with Eldengbao and others he took Shilong Mountain and beheaded the rebel chieftain Shi Liudeng; he was enfeoffed as a third-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the rebels repeatedly; with Eldengbao he took Shilong Mountain and killed rebel chief Shi Liudeng, and was enfeoffed as a third-class baron.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，諡恪靖，祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, was given the posthumous title Kejing, and enshrined in the Hall of Worthy Officials.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year, was posthumously titled Kejing, "Respectful and Tranquil," and enshrined in the Hall of Worthy Officials.

sentences.zh: 四年，追論在湖北軍中受餽白金四千，罷祀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was retrospectively judged for accepting four thousand taels of silver while in the army in Hubei, and his shrine worship was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was posthumously condemned for accepting four thousand taels of silver in the Hubei army, and his shrine honors were revoked.

sentences.zh: 舒亮，蘇佳氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Shu Liang, of the Sujia clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Liang, of the Sujia clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 自前鋒累遷參領。

translations.literal: From the vanguard he rose in succession to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the vanguard to company commander.

sentences.zh: 師徵金川，舒亮從副都統齊里克齊率健銳營為裨將。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Jinchuan, Shu Liang followed Vice Commander Qilikeqi, leading the Vanguard Camp as deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinchuan campaign Shu Liang served under Vice Commander Qilikeqi as deputy leader of the Vanguard Camp.

sentences.zh: 攻穆谷，舒亮伏山下待賊，殺賊甚眾。

translations.literal: In the attack on Mugu, Shu Liang lay in ambush below the mountain waiting for the rebels and killed a great many.
translations.idiomatic: At Mugu he ambushed the rebels below the mountain and killed many.

sentences.zh: 攻卡角，賊匿山溝，舒亮於密箐中望見火光，以火器就擊之，賊驚潰。

translations.literal: In the attack on Kajiao the rebels hid in mountain ravines; Shu Liang saw firelight in a dense thicket and struck at it with firearms; the rebels fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: At Kajiao rebels hid in ravines; Shu Liang spotted firelight in a thicket, fired into it, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 以功，累遷鑲黃旗滿洲副都統。
