translations.literal: For merit he rose in succession to vice commander of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: For his merits he was promoted to vice commander of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 從克噶拉依，賜穆騰額巴圖魯名號。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Gela'i and was granted the title Muteng'e Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: He helped capture Gela'i and received the title Muteng'e Baturu.

sentences.zh: 師還，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: When the army returned his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign his portrait entered the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十六年，大學士阿桂討撒拉爾亂回蘇四十三，舒亮從。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year of the Qianlong reign Grand Secretary Agui suppressed the Salar rebel Su Forty-three; Shu Liang followed him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1781 Grand Secretary Agui suppressed the Salar rebel Su Forty-three; Shu Liang followed him.

sentences.zh: 初至，破賊華林山。

translations.literal: On first arrival he defeated the rebels at Hualin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he defeated the rebels at Hualin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 賊掘濠設卡以自固。

translations.literal: The rebels dug moats and set checkpoints to fortify themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dug moats and set checkpoints to hold their ground.

sentences.zh: 阿桂令海蘭察自山西攻賊卡，舒亮自南山進，當賊鋒，賊競出，射舒亮，傷左股，舒亮拔箭裹創，复戰，奪賊卡四，殺賊百餘。

translations.literal: Agui ordered Hailancha to attack the rebel checkpoints from the west while Shu Liang advanced from the south hill and met the rebel front; the rebels all rushed out and shot Shu Liang, wounding his left thigh; Shu Liang pulled out the arrow, bound the wound, and fought again, taking four rebel checkpoints and killing more than a hundred rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Agui sent Hailancha against the rebel checkpoints from the west while Shu Liang advanced from the south and took the brunt; rebels shot him in the left thigh; he pulled out the arrow, bound the wound, fought on, took four checkpoints, and killed more than a hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 又與海蘭察诇賊不備，以土囊填濠渡軍，殲守濠賊，复奪十餘卡。

translations.literal: Again with Hailancha he spied out the rebels' unpreparedness, filled the moat with earth bags to cross the army, destroyed the rebels guarding the moat, and again took more than ten checkpoints.
translations.idiomatic: With Hailancha he caught the rebels off guard, filled the moat with earth bags to cross, wiped out the moat guards, and took more than ten checkpoints.

sentences.zh: 蘇四十三既誅，复剿華林寺餘匪。

translations.literal: After Su Forty-three was executed he again suppressed the remaining bandits at Hualin Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Forty-three was killed he mopped up the remnants at Hualin Temple.

sentences.zh: 事平，還京師。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion ended he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 林爽文之亂，福康安出視師，舒亮以正黃旗護軍統領為領隊大臣。

translations.literal: In Lin Shuangwen's rebellion Fuk'anggan went out to take command, and Shu Liang served as leading minister in the capacity of commander of the Plain Yellow Banner guards.
translations.idiomatic: During Lin Shuangwen's rebellion Fuk'anggan took command, and Shu Liang served as leading minister as commander of the Plain Yellow Banner guards.

sentences.zh: 至台灣，福康安軍道笨港救嘉義，令舒亮出別道分賊勢。

translations.literal: On reaching Taiwan Fuk'anggan led his army by the Bengang route to relieve Jiayi and ordered Shu Liang out by a separate route to divide the rebel strength.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiwan Fuk'anggan marched through Bengang to relieve Jiayi and sent Shu Liang by a separate route to split the rebel force.

sentences.zh: 賊方據北大肚山拒我，舒亮迎擊，敗之，連破南大肚、王田、瀨湑、半山、坑子諸莊，遂克烏日莊。

translations.literal: The rebels were holding Beidadu Mountain to resist us; Shu Liang met them in attack and defeated them, in succession broke Nandadu, Wangtian, Laixu, Banshan, Kengzi, and other villages, and then took Wuri Village.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held Beidadu Mountain; Shu Liang attacked, defeated them, took Nandadu, Wangtian, Laixu, Banshan, Kengzi, and other villages in succession, and captured Wuri Village.

sentences.zh: 會福康安軍夾擊，解嘉義圍。

translations.literal: Joining Fuk'anggan's army in a pincer attack, the siege of Jiayi was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Joining Fuk'anggan in a pincer attack, they lifted the siege of Jiayi.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，爽文竄匿東勢角。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year Shuangwen fled into hiding at Dongshijiao.
translations.idiomatic: In 1788 Shuangwen hid at Dongshijiao.

sentences.zh: 福康安督舒亮等追逮，令舒亮直取東勢角，山徑峻險，將卒皆步上，殺賊二千餘。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan directed Shu Liang and others in pursuit and ordered Shu Liang to take Dongshijiao directly; the mountain paths were steep and perilous, officers and soldiers all climbed on foot, and more than two thousand rebels were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan sent Shu Liang and others in pursuit and ordered Shu Liang to take Dongshijiao directly; on steep mountain paths the troops climbed on foot and killed more than two thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 爽文复走老衢峙，舒亮督諸軍急進，獲之，亂遂定。

translations.literal: Shuangwen again fled to Laoquzhi; Shu Liang directed the armies in rapid advance and captured him; the rebellion was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen fled again to Laoquzhi; Shu Liang pressed forward with the armies and captured him, ending the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 上以台灣遠在海外，主客民雜處，風俗素悍，命於府城及嘉義立諸將帥生祠，示威德。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering that Taiwan lay far overseas, that settlers and natives were mixed, and that local customs were by nature fierce, ordered living shrines to the commanders erected at the prefectural seat and at Jiayi to display imperial authority and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Because Taiwan lay far overseas, settlers and natives were mixed, and the region was notoriously unruly, the emperor ordered living shrines to the generals built at the prefectural seat and Jiayi to display imperial power and virtue.

sentences.zh: 祠成，命並及在事疆吏，首福康安，次海蘭察、李侍堯、普爾普、鄂輝、徐嗣曾，而以舒亮殿焉。

translations.literal: When the shrines were completed he ordered that frontier officials involved in the affair also be included: first Fuk'anggan, then Hailancha, Li Shiyao, Pu'erpu, E Hui, and Xu Sizeng, with Shu Liang bringing up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: When the shrines were finished he included the frontier officials involved: Fuk'anggan first, then Hailancha, Li Shiyao, Pu'erpu, E Hui, and Xu Sizeng, with Shu Liang last.

sentences.zh: 尋授鑲紅旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed commander of the Mongol Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed commander of the Mongol Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 師還，命監爽文及其徒賴大等生致京師。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was ordered to supervise the delivery alive to the capital of Shuangwen and his follower Lai Da and others.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was ordered to escort Shuangwen and his follower Lai Da alive to the capital.

sentences.zh: 賴大道病，舒亮令誅之，不稱上意，命仍為護軍統領。

translations.literal: Lai Da fell ill on the road; Shu Liang ordered him executed, which did not accord with the emperor's intent, and he was ordered to remain commander of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Da fell ill en route; Shu Liang had him executed, displeasing the emperor, and was kept on as guards commander.

sentences.zh: 敘功，予雲騎尉世職，再圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; he was given the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain and again had his portrait placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: His merits were recorded; he received the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain and again entered the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 出為荊州、黑龍江將軍。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as general at Jingzhou and Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as general at Jingzhou and Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 在黑龍江，坐私市貂皮，奪官，削世職。

translations.literal: At Heilongjiang he was punished for privately trading sable furs; his office was taken and his hereditary rank revoked.
translations.idiomatic: At Heilongjiang he was dismissed for illegal sable trade and lost his hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 川、陝、楚教匪起，命以三等侍衛從軍。

translations.literal: When sect rebels rose in Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Hubei he was ordered to join the army as a third-rank bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: When White Lotus rebels rose in Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Hubei he was sent to the army as a third-rank guardsman.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，戰襄陽，再戰劉家集，屢俘斬賊渠。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Jiaqing reign he fought at Xiangyang, fought again at Liujiaji, and repeatedly captured and beheaded rebel chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaqing he fought at Xiangyang and Liujiaji and repeatedly captured or killed rebel chiefs.

sentences.zh: 攻當陽，先登，額中槍，奮進，殺賊千餘，獲其酋，遂克當陽，賜孔雀翎，授鑲藍旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: In the attack on Dangyang he was first to scale the wall; a bullet struck his forehead, yet he pressed forward fiercely, killed more than a thousand rebels, captured their chieftain, and thus took Dangyang; he was granted the peacock feather and appointed vice commander of the Han Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: At Dangyang he was first over the wall; shot in the forehead, he pressed on, killed more than a thousand rebels, captured their chief, and took the city; he received the peacock feather and was made vice commander of the Han Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 賊自鍾祥分竄唐、鄧，設伏呂堰驛，西竄賊殲焉；

translations.literal: The rebels split from Zhongxiang and fled separately toward Tang and Deng; he set an ambush at Luyan Post, and the western fleeing rebels were destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: Rebels fleeing from Zhongxiang split toward Tang and Deng; he ambushed them at Luyan Post and destroyed the western band;

sentences.zh: 乃合兵逐東竄賊，戰草店，復中槍，賚銀絲盒、荷包。

translations.literal: he then combined forces to pursue the eastern fleeing rebels, fought at Caodian, was again shot, and was bestowed a silver-thread box and purse.
translations.idiomatic: he then pursued the eastern band, fought at Caodian, was shot again, and received a silver-thread box and purse.

sentences.zh: 旋以縱賊渡滾河，奪孔雀翎、巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because he had allowed rebels to cross the Gun River, his peacock feather and Baturu title were taken away.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he lost his peacock feather and Baturu title for letting rebels cross the Gun River.

sentences.zh: 二年，坐賊渡漢江，降三品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the second year, because rebels crossed the Han River, he was reduced to third-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year rebels crossed the Han River, and he was demoted to third-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 三年，復以總督勒保劾勦賊不力，奪官，以兵丁留軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was again impeached by Governor-General Lebao for ineffective suppression of rebels; his office was taken and he remained with the army as a common soldier.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Governor-General Lebao impeached him for slack pursuit of rebels; he was stripped of rank and kept in the army as a common soldier.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：林爽文亂起，常青及福州將軍恆瑞並水陸二提督，躬率師東渡，徘徊坐誤。

translations.literal: The commentary says: When Lin Shuangwen's rebellion broke out, Chang Qing together with the Fuzhou general Heng Rui and the two land and naval commanders personally led armies east across the sea, yet hesitated and sat by while opportunities were lost.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators observe: When Lin Shuangwen rebelled, Chang Qing, Fuzhou General Heng Rui, and the land and naval commanders crossed to Taiwan in person yet dithered and let the crisis worsen.

sentences.zh: 高宗爵柴大紀，誅郝壯猷，欲以激勵諸將；

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong ennobled Chai Daji and executed Hao Zhuangyou, intending thereby to spur the other commanders;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong ennobled Chai Daji and executed Hao Zhuangyou to spur the other generals;

sentences.zh: 繼以元枚代，功未竟而卒，終煩禁旅，始克底定。

translations.literal: Yuanmei was then sent to replace him, but before merit was achieved he died; in the end it required the imperial guard to arrive before the affair could be brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Yuanmei replaced him but died before finishing the work; only when imperial guards arrived was the rebellion finally suppressed.

sentences.zh: 承平久，水陸諸軍不足用，不得獨為大紀罪也。

translations.literal: After long peace the land and naval forces were inadequate; Daji alone cannot be blamed.
translations.idiomatic: After long peace the land and naval forces had grown inadequate; Daji alone cannot bear all the blame.

sentences.zh: 鄂輝、舒亮從福康安出師，與攀龍、朝雄皆有戰績；

translations.literal: E Hui and Shu Liang followed Fuk'anggan in campaign, as did Panlong and Chaoxiong, all with battle merit;
translations.idiomatic: E Hui and Shu Liang campaigned under Fuk'anggan, as did Panlong and Chaoxiong, all with solid records;

sentences.zh: 然大紀力保危城，當時聲譽遠出諸將上。

translations.literal: yet Daji had strenuously held a perilous city, and at the time his reputation far exceeded that of the other commanders.
translations.idiomatic: yet Daji had held a desperate city through sheer effort, and at the time his reputation far outshone the other generals.

sentences.zh: 功名之際，有幸有不幸，固如是夫！

translations.literal: In the matter of fame and achievement there is fortune and misfortune; it is indeed so!
translations.idiomatic: In the pursuit of fame and merit, fortune and misfortune go hand in hand—such is the way of things!
